key_insight: The anomalous γ-loop in Fe–Cr alloys arises from competing magnetic, vibrational and chemical effects that change how Cr stabilizes fcc versus bcc structures.
engineering_relevance: Modeling these coupled effects can improve predictions of phase stability and transformation temperatures in Fe–Cr alloy design.
method: Coupled atomistic spin dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics.
Used thermodynamic integration to calculate fcc–bcc Gibbs free-energy differences.
Compared static magnetically ordered and disordered states to isolate magnetic effects.
evidence_signal: Simulations at 0, 5, 10 and 15 at.% Cr over 800–1800 K reproduced the experimental γ-loop qualitatively, with near-quantitative accuracy for the γ–δ transition.
watch_item: The α–γ transition temperatures were underestimated by approximately 200 K, and clustering as a cause of loop closure remains tentative.
paper_title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
